prompt: A hotel renovated half its rooms. Renovated rooms sell for 25% more per night and are 70% full, against 80% full for the old rooms. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The renovated rooms are probably earning less than the old ones.
options.feedback: 1.25 × 70% = 87.5 against 80 for the old rooms, so renovated rooms earn about 9% more per available room.

options.text: Price, booking channels, room features and guest mix may all be at work.
options.feedback: This lists causes without committing to one.

options.text: The higher rate likely more than makes up for the lower occupancy.
options.feedback: Right. 1.25 × 70% = 87.5 against 80, so renovated rooms earn about 9% more per available room. I'd check revenue per available room by room type over a full season.

options.text: Guests probably prefer the old rooms' style.
options.feedback: Renovated rooms are 70% full at a 25% premium, so demand for them is strong.

explanation: The data shows renovated rooms earning 1.25 × 70% = 87.5 per available room against 80 for old rooms, about 9% more. Likely conclusion: the higher rate more than makes up for lower occupancy. To test it, compare revenue per available room by room type over a full season. If occupancy drops further off-peak, the gain could disappear.
